scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Plug in a fast charger, and your phone races to half in minutes. Then the last bit crawls. But why?

scenes.name: power
scenes.text: Charging speed is power. Power is voltage times current. Push either one up, and more energy flows each second.

scenes.name: talk
scenes.text: When you plug in, the phone and charger talk over the cable, using a standard like USB Power Delivery.

scenes.name: volt
scenes.text: They agree on a higher voltage, say nine volts instead of five, so more watts flow through the same cable.

scenes.name: chip
scenes.text: A charging chip in the phone converts it down to what the battery needs, about four volts, at a high current.

scenes.name: taper
scenes.text: Near eighty percent, the battery is getting full, so the chip lowers the current to protect it. That's why the last stretch is slower.

scenes.name: heat
scenes.text: Sensors watch the temperature too. If the phone gets hot, charging slows down automatically.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Handshake, voltage, chip, taper. Fast first, then careful. Follow for more on how things really work.
